ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Heimlich, a Satmar follower who studies at a yeshiva in Elad, had been detained after approaching military authorities to regularise his status. The case comes amid a long-running dispute over military service for Israel’s ultra-Orthodox community. The original arrangement dates to 1948, when Israeli Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion approved an exemption for 400 yeshiva students. It later expanded significantly. In 2023, the legal framework for the broad exemption expired, and Israel’s Supreme Court ruled in 2024 that the state must begin enforcing conscription. The issue has become more contentious as Israel faces prolonged military demands. https://www.politico.eu/article/parliame.text: BRUSSELS — Three of the European Parliament's biggest political groups say they will fight an EU proposal to relax carbon pricing rules, opening a rift that could push conservative lawmakers to side with the far right to weaken the bloc's climate ambition. The center-left Socialists and Democrats, the centrist Renew Europe and the Greens all said in recent days that they would try to preserve an ambitious path to net zero under the Emissions Trading System, forcing heavy industry to cut planet-warming emissions faster than Brussels proposes. That puts them at odds with the center-right European People's Party, Parliament's biggest group, which broadly supports the European Commission's proposal. Advertisement Advertisement For years, those four groups have worked together in Parliament to pass legislation that strikes a political middle ground, shunning collaboration with the far right. The sometimes uneasy alliance has ensured consistent, bipartisan support for the ETS, Europe’s most powerful tool for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. But now, a reform of the landmark cap-and-trade scheme, unveiled by the EU executive in July , looks set to become a bellwether in an era when, increasingly, the center no longer holds. The EPP is steering Parliament’s work on the proposed ETS revision through veteran German lawmaker Peter Liese, who wants to find a deal that satisfies everyone. “I don’t want the Venezuelan majority. It’s against my convictions, but it is also not possible because nobody would see [Marine] Le Pen, the Austrian far-right FPÖ or the German extreme-far-right AfD voting for any ETS proposal,” he told POLITICO in September, using the informal term for a controversial alliance of center-right and far-right groups. Instead, Liese, who maintains close ties with Dutch S&D lawmaker Mohammed Chahim, said he wanted “the broadest possible coalition,” including the right-wing European Conservatives and Reformists as well as “the Greens, The Left, if they want.” But new amendments filed last week by the S&D, the second-largest group in Parliament, as well as the Greens and Renew, point to major schisms over key aspects of the ETS reform. The biggest divide concerns the so-called linear reduction factor, the mechanism that determines how quickly the supply of pollution permits shrinks each year. Advertisement Advertisement Under the current trajectory, the total cap on carbon emissions for all sectors covered by the ETS falls slightly each year, and would reach zero around 2039 or 2040. At that point, ETS sectors — which include power generators, steelmakers and chemical manufacturers — would no longer be able to emit any carbon dioxide at all. Liese’s proposal would push that date into the 2040s, in line with the Commission’s original pitch in the summer. But the three other centrist or left-leaning groups oppose the plan and have tabled nearly identical amendments that would keep the rates high until the end of next decade and bring about quicker industrial decarbonization across Europe. Though the percentages between the warring groups appear tiny, they translate into millions of additional tons of CO₂ emissions and expose a growing political gulf. S&D, the Greens and Renew are fighting to preserve Europe’s climate ambitions, while the EPP is increasingly sympathetic to the concerns of the chemicals and metals industries, both of which have been vocally critical of the ETS. MEPs vote during a session in the hemicycle in Strasbourg on April 28, 2026. | Jean-Christophe Verhaegen/AFP via Getty Images But just as the chances for a centrist compromise dim, Liese has another possible route. Memories of fascism in the early twentieth century once discouraged mainstream political groups from working with the far right. That firewall appeared to erode when talks with centrist allies collapsed in 2025 over the first omnibus package governing certain environmental reporting rules. The EPP turned to the right-wing ECR and the far-right Patriots for Europe and Europe of Sovereign Nations to secure a deal , paving the way for similar alliances in the future. On the ETS, there is a growing risk that it could happen all over again. Advertisement Advertisement Czech lawmaker Alexandr Vondra of the ECR recently floated the possibility of working with Liese to secure a deal backed by his right-wing group during a parliamentary debate on the ETS. “I would address here specifically EPP because it holds the key to the success of the reform of the ETS system,” he said, before laying out a list of industry-friendly demands that included a much looser trajectory to zero emissions. “If so, count me and my group in.” Amendments tabled by Vondra this week and seen by POLITICO reflected a similar willingness to work with the EPP and limited regard for emissions reductions. If Liese does decide to shift his compromise to the right and cashes in on ECR votes, it could also quell problems within his own party. The Polish, Spanish and Italian branches of the EPP are all unhappy with what they see as Liese's overly climate-friendly proposal, according to three parliamentary insiders. Recent votes in Parliament on the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, the bloc’s carbon levy on imports that works in tandem with the ETS, exposed fractures within the group, with portions of the EPP supporting right-wing groups or abstaining on a key provision of the legislation. But how willing far-right groups will be to play ball with the EPP remains to be seen. The Europe of Sovereign Nations group — whose members include Germany's far-right Alternative für Deutschland — is hostile to the ETS and wants it totally abolished. But the Patriots — whose members include France's National Rally — might provide Liese with an opening: the group generally calls for the policy to be slowed to a halt , especially the upcoming ETS2, as it does all Green Deal legislation . French far-right lawmaker and rising political star Jordan Bardella said as much in a speech to Parliament in May. “ETS: three letters, an acronym that reeks of detached bureaucracy, with one question that keeps coming up: who’s going to pay?” he said . https://www.dw.com/en/populist-czech-pm-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5ONFe Babis has been described as 'Trumpist' in his outlook Image: Beata Zawrzel/ZUMA/IMAGO Advertisement The ruling coalition of populist billionaire Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis has failed to win a single seat in elections in the Senate . The result means pro-Western opposition parties control the chamber, the upper house of parliament. The election on Saturday was the first electoral test for Babis after he won parliamentary elections in October 2025 that returned him to power after a break of four years since his first term as premier. What happened in the Czech Senate elections? Final results from the two-day ballot showed that candidates directly linked to the opposition parties won 22 of the 27 seats up for grabs in the 81-member Senate, retaining a previous opposition majority. The centrist ANO (or YES) movement led by Babis failed to win any more seats, leaving it with 14 Senate lawmakers. Babis called the result "catastrophic." "We certainly didn't expect that we wouldn't win a single Senate seat in this election," he said, but vowed to nonetheless go ahead with his government's agenda. That includes an unpopular plan to revamp funding for the country’s public broadcasters. Czech journalists warn of dangers of public media reform To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video His euroskeptic coalition has also ended direct military support for Ukraine as it defends itself against a Russian invasion, and opposed European Union policies to combat global warming. Although the lower house of the Czech parliament plays the main legislative role, the Senate has a big say in passing constitutional amendments and approving Constitutional Court judges. Read Ethiopia ranked “Not Free” in freedom house’s 2026 report with a dismal score of 30 By Our Staff Reporter October 26, 2026 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Ethiopia remains categorized as “Not Free” in the latest Freedom on the Net 2026 report by Freedom House, reflecting ongoing concerns over prolonged internet disruptions, restrictions on digital expression, and systemic barriers to online rights. ​Ethiopia earned a score of 30 out of 100 in the annual assessment, placing it among the lowest-rated nations among the 38 countries evaluated. The report, titled Seismic Shifts on the Global Internet, covers developments between June 1, 2025, and May 31, 2026, measuring access to the internet, availability of information, and freedom of expression without state interference. ​The low rating underscores a growing divergence between Ethiopia’s expanding digital infrastructure and its protection of user rights. While expanding connectivity remains critical for economic development, financial inclusion, and public service delivery, Freedom House noted that persistent connectivity restrictions continue to disrupt basic communication and economic activity. ​A key focus of the report’s regional analysis is Ethiopia’s history of localized connectivity blackouts. The assessment highlights the extensive telecommunications shutdown imposed in the Tigray region following the outbreak of conflict in November 2020. Lasting over two years, it remains the longest subnational blackout recorded in the report’s history. ​Freedom House detailed how prolonged service disruptions hindered humanitarian aid operations, restricted media reporting, and hampered basic family communications. The report also cataloged other major historical disruptions across the country, including an 818-day blackout in Tigray, a 347-day disruption in Amhara starting in August 2023, and earlier multi-month blackouts in Oromia. These figures encompass both total blackouts and targeted mobile or broadband throttlings during periods of political tension or conflict. ​Within Africa, Ethiopia’s score of 30 ranks behind nations such as Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, and The Gambia. Under Freedom House’s methodology, scores below 40 denote a “Not Free” environment, 40 to 69 indicates “Partly Free,” and 70 to 100 signifies “Free.” ​Freedom House reported that global internet freedom declined for the 16th consecutive year, with conditions deteriorating in 16 of the 38 monitored nations. Estonia retained its position as the world’s most open digital environment with a score of 91, while China and Myanmar remained the most restrictive. ​Beyond network shutdowns, the 2026 report identified emerging global challenges to digital rights, including the misuse of artificial intelligence for content manipulation and overly broad online safety regulations. While the report does not accuse Ethiopia of adopting specific invasive AI or age-verification laws, it cautions that such regulatory frameworks pose growing risks to privacy and press freedom worldwide. ​Freedom House calls for governments to uphold open internet access, implement independent oversight on digital surveillance, and ensure all online restrictions remain transparent, proportionate, and legally justified. https://www.portfolio.hu/global/20261109.text: Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök arra figyelmeztette európai szövetségeseit, hogy Oroszország a Dnyeper folyón átívelő hidak módszeres lerombolására készül - írja a Financial Times . A támadások célja az ország kettévágása, a katonai utánpótlási vonalak elvágása, valamint az energiaellátás megbénítása a téli hónapok előtt, miközben a felek az Egyesült Államok és az Európai Unió részvételével Abu-Dzabiban ülnek tárgyalóasztalhoz. Az ukrán államfő Ursula von der Leyennel, az Európai Bizottság elnökével folytatott telefonbeszélgetése során osztotta meg aggodalmait. A megbeszélés részleteit ismerő források szerint Moszkva el akarja szigetelni az ország Oroszországgal határos keleti részét az Európai Unióval szomszédos nyugati területektől. A terv nemcsak a fizikai elszigetelésre irányul, hanem a nyugatról keletre tartó áramellátás megszakítására is, ami emberek millióit hagyná fűtés és világítás nélkül a tél közepén. A kialakult helyzetre reagálva az Európai Unió egy speciális vészhelyzeti mechanizmus aktiválásáról döntött, hogy gyors pénzügyi segítséget nyújtson a legszükségesebb kiadásokra. A folyamatos csapások miatt ugyanis több régióban – köztük Kijevben, Dnyipróban, Szumiban, Donyeckben és Herszonban – már most is súlyos fennakadások tapasztalhatók az áram-, víz- és távhőszolgáltatásban. A két vezető egyeztetése közvetlenül megelőzte a kedden és szerdán Abu-Dzabiban zajló békekonferenciát, amelyen Kijev, Moszkva, Washington és az EU tisztviselői vesznek részt. Ezek a háromoldalú egyeztetések február vége óta szüneteltek, amikor a Trump-adminisztráció háborút indított Irán ellen. A tárgyalások előtt von der Leyen ismét biztosította támogatásáról Zelenszkij azon kezdeményezését, amely az élelmiszer- és energia-infrastruktúrát érintő tűzszünetet sürgeti. Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnök környezetéből származó információk szerint azonban a Kreml a mostani csapásokat válaszlépésnek tekinti az orosz energetikai és logisztikai hálózatok elleni ukrán támadásokért. A Dnyeper stratégiai jelentőségű vízi út, amely észak-déli irányban szeli át az országot, délen pedig természetes frontvonalat képez a szemben álló felek között. Oroszország október óta egyre intenzívebben támadja a folyó átkelőit, ballisztikus rakétákkal és sugárhajtású drónokkal többek között a kijevi Északi és Déli hidat is eltalálták, megrongálva a tartópilléreket és az útpályát. A csaknem négymillió lakosú főváros két partját mindössze nyolc híd köti össze, így egyetlen átkelő kiesése is súlyos közlekedési káoszt okoz, ahogy az a szombati támadás után is történt. Kijev térségén kívül ráadásul nagyon kevés használható híd maradt, a legközelebbi átkelési lehetőséget az északra fekvő kijevi, valamint a 130 kilométerre délre található kanyivi vízerőművek gátjai jelentik. Katonai elemzők szerint az átkelők megrongálása jelentősen megnehezíti a keleti fronton harcoló ukrán egységek utánpótlását. Franz-Stefan Gady bécsi katonai szakértő rámutatott, hogy a nehézfegyverzetet és a nagy mennyiségű lőszert főként vasúton szállítják, így a vasúti hidak kiesése lelassítja a tartalékok átcsoportosítását a veszélyeztetett frontszakaszokra. Bár Kijev pontonhidak építésével enyhíthet a helyzeten, az orosz cél elsősorban a felőrlés, valamint az, hogy az ukrán hadvezetést a szűkös légvédelmi kapacitások szétaprózására kényszerítse. Ukrajna védekezését súlyosan nehezíti az amerikai gyártmányú Patriot elfogórakéták hiánya, ugyanis jelenleg ez az egyetlen olyan eszköz az ukrán arzenálban, amellyel megbízhatóan megsemmisíthetők az orosz ballisztikus rakéták. Az iráni háború miatt kialakult globális készlethiány következtében azonban sem Washington, sem az európai szövetségesek nem szívesen válnak meg saját tartalékaiktól. A helyzetet tovább súlyosbítja, hogy Szerhij Beszkresztnov, az ukrán elnök tanácsadója szerint az orosz rakétákat új, fejlett irányítórendszerrel szerelték fel. A címlapkép illusztráció.
